text: Put one lakh rupees into India's highway trust, and toll roads pay you every quarter. But there is a catch nobody tells you.
National Highways Infrah Trust, or N H I T, owns toll roads monetised by N H A I. Every time a truck pays toll, part of that cash flows to unit holders.
At one hundred and sixty nine rupees a unit, one lakh rupees buys about five hundred and ninety one units.
For the June quarter, it paid three rupees and nineteen paise per unit. That is about one thousand eight hundred and eighty rupees on your one lakh.
For the September quarter, it declared two rupees fifty three. About one thousand four hundred and ninety five rupees. So the payout changes every quarter.
Most of it is interest, so it is taxed at your income tax slab.
Now the catch. N H I T is a privately placed trust. On N S E, it trades in lots of twenty five thousand units. At today's price, that is about forty two lakh rupees.
So with one lakh, you simply cannot buy it on the exchange. Public in-vits, like N H A I's newer Raajmarg trust, trade one unit at a time.
Would you buy highway income? Comment ROAD, and save this.
